Home / Publications

Publications

Research in higher education, business and language assessment.

Journal articles

2026

Outsiders within: Exploring integration strategies of international faculty in Chinese higher education institutions

Ding, J., Yang, L., & Mlynarski, J.

Higher Education · Published 13 August 2026

Impact factor 4.3 (2025)Q1Scopus

PublisherDOI

International faculty (IF) are increasingly recruited to Chinese universities to support knowledge transfer and internationalisation, yet they frequently report experiencing persistent marginal positions. This study examines how IF in Chinese higher education navigate this marginal status. Drawing on thirty semi-structured interviews, we identify five reflexive tactics: playing by the rules, contextual collaboration, negotiating around the rules, tactical non-pursuit, and strategic self-detachment.

These tactics are deployed across four domains of institutional integration: cultural norms, interpersonal relations, resources, and academic practice. By foregrounding reflexivity, the analysis reframes integration not as a binary outcome of assimilation or marginalisation, but as a non-linear decision-making process mediated by ethical judgement.

The study reveals that integration encompasses not only intercultural competence and resource allocation, but also a strategic balancing of selective engagement and detachment, driven by distinct ethical foci. Findings underscore the value of more inclusive institutional cultures and greater tolerance for outsider-within positions.

2026

Reconsidering Internationalisation: Navigating the Challenges of Chinese Private Higher Education Institutions

Ding, J., & Mlynarski, J.

Higher Education Forum · Volume 23 · pp. 183–208

Q4 (2025)Scopus

PublisherDOI

This study examines the internationalisation of Chinese private higher education institutions (CPHEIs). It addresses a notable gap in the literature which has primarily focused on public universities. Drawing from qualitative case studies of five CPHEIs in Shaanxi Province, this study examines the key rationales, challenges and strategies deployed by CPHEIs and identifies emerging opportunities within the Asian higher education landscape.

The findings reveal that CPHEIs employ an inward-oriented internationalisation, not to pursue global prestige, but to reform internal governance, enhance students’ employability, and secure financial resilience. Those strategies include intra-regional collaboration within Asia, the pursuit of discipline-specific accreditations, and the integration of international resources into institutional development.

This study provides insights into the internationalisation processes and practices of CPHEIs through the lens of an extended global agency heuristic theory, with potential broader relevance for similar private institutions in China and abroad.

Building Brand Equity: The Impact of Brand Experience, Brand Love, and Brand Engagement—A Case Study of Customers’ Perception of the Apple Brand in China

Sohaib, M., Mlynarski, J., & Wu, R.

Sustainability · Volume 15(1) · Article 746

Impact factor 4.1 (2025)Q2Scopus

PublisherDOI

Regardless of a customer’s social status, wealth, or country of origin, Apple products have been notorious for establishing trends in regard to electronic devices. As of 2019, China accounted for 17% percent of all Apple sales. This has been made possible in large part due to Chinese customers’ favorable image of the Apple brand and the positive experience with Apple products. This study aimed to examine the impact of brand experience, brand love, and brand engagement on brand equity.

The brand-love mediation role between brand experience and brand engagement/brand equity was also explored. The conceptual framework was supported by social exchange and attribution theories. According to the analysis of 339 respondents from China, brand experience, brand love, and brand engagement significantly positively affects Apple’s brand equity. Additionally, it was discovered that brand love demonstrates a significant mediating role between brand experience and brand engagement/brand equity.

These findings can aid other manufacturers offering similar electronic products in China to adapt their marketing and competitive strategies in order to boost their brand equity and as a result sales revenue.

Vocabulary Size Assessment as a Predictor of Plagiarism

Dodigovic, M., Mlynarski, J., & Wei, R.

In Current Issues in Language Evaluation, Assessment and Testing: Research and Practice · Cambridge Scholars Publishing · pp. 222–235

Publisher

Culture, education, attitude and language proficiency have been viewed as the major causes of second language writer plagiarism (Amsberry, 2009; Erkaya, 2009). However, research data that would sufficiently substantiate these claims are scarce. The study described in this chapter investigates the relationship between plagiarism and vocabulary knowledge in the writing of over 200 students of English as a second language. It uses both lexical error and vocabulary size assessment as measures of vocabulary command. The study relies on an instructional software tool called Grammarly, which identifies both textual borrowing and language errors, as well as on the Vocabulary Size Test (VST) to measure students’ vocabulary knowledge. The results indicate that there is some correlation between the error count and plagiarism, and a strong negative correlation between vocabulary size and plagiarism rate. Therefore, the findings seem to suggest that poor vocabulary command could be a major cause of plagiarism in second language writers. Based on these findings, the importance of systematic vocabulary teaching and learning as a strategy to avoid plagiarism emerges.

Lecturer · School of Business Administration

I am a lecturer and project coordinator at Xi’an Eurasia University. I have approximately 17 years of experience in education in China, spanning university teaching, curriculum development and academic leadership.

I teach Statistics, Corporate Finance, Project Management, management, human resource management and organisational behaviour. I have also taught English for Academic Purposes and research methods within international university preparation programmes.

My academic leadership experience includes serving as an Academic Principal and leading NCUK programmes and centres. My responsibilities have included academic operations, programme development, assessment, staff development and supporting students’ progression to overseas universities.

Research and academic development. My published work examines international faculty integration in Chinese universities, internationalisation in private higher education, brand equity and vocabulary assessment in relation to plagiarism. My academic development work includes curriculum standards, quality assurance and EFMD EPAS accreditation planning.

statistics.title: Statistics · Jacob Mlynarski
statistics.description: Learn to describe data, compare variation and work through probability problems, one concept at a time.
statistics.content:
Home / Courses / Statistics

Statistics with Project Skills

Foundation · Business & Science · Semester 1

Practice for Exam
Course InfoWhat You Will LearnCourse Content

About Course

Statistics helps us turn data into evidence. In this 12-week foundation course, you will learn how to collect reliable data, summarise a dataset, present results clearly and use probability to understand uncertainty.

We begin with the calculations needed for statistics, then move through sampling, descriptive measures, charts and Excel. Later topics introduce probability distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and regression, using examples from business and science.

Each concept follows a clear sequence: a worked demonstration, guided practice and an independent task. You will practise calculations, interpret what the answers mean and explain your conclusions in plain English.

What Will You Learn?

  • Choose sampling methods and recognise bias.
  • Describe the centre, spread and shape of data.
  • Build and interpret statistical charts in Excel.
  • Calculate probabilities and use distribution models.
  • Estimate population values and test claims.
  • Interpret correlation and regression results.

Course Content

12 weeks · 40 classes

Every class lasts 90 minutes. Class D tutorials take place in Weeks 2, 5, 8 and 11.

Week 01 · Mathematical foundations3 classes
A

Class A · Numbers and counting

Build the mathematical toolkit for statistics: use set notation and Venn diagrams, select counting methods, classify numbers and calculate accurately using PEMDAS.

90 min
B

Class B · Calculations in context

Solve linear and simple quadratic equations, convert units, and use percentages and ratios to make and justify numerical decisions.

90 min
C

Class C · Applied problem solving

Apply the Week 1 toolkit to a connected product case, from customer evidence and product choices to packaging, material quantities and sales revenue.

90 min
Week 02 · Sampling and collecting data4 classes
A

Class A · Populations, samples and variables

Identify the group being studied, distinguish sample statistics from population parameters, classify data and carry out simple random or systematic selection.

90 min
B

Class B · Sampling methods and survey bias

Develop stratified and cluster sampling plans, distinguish chance variation from bias, and evaluate the reliability and practical cost of survey evidence.

90 min
C

Class C · Survey workshop

Investigate a canteen survey, check whether its claims follow from the data, repair its sampling and measurement methods, and write a defensible report.

90 min
D

Class D · Tutorial: review, repair and prepare

Review numerical skills and sampling, revisit difficult steps and prepare for assessment.

90 min
Week 03 · Descriptive statistics3 classes
A

Class A · Centre, spread and distribution shape

Mean, median and mode; range, quartiles using n + 1, IQR and five-number summaries; interpret skewness and the effect of extreme values.

90 min
B

Class B · Understanding variation

Deviations, population and sample variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and kurtosis; calculate and interpret absolute and relative spread.

90 min
C

Class C · Paper supplier workshop

Compare two suppliers using delivery-time averages, IQR, sample SD and CV; justify decisions for routine orders and changing deadlines. Formative Assessment 1 follows the workshop.

90 min
Week 04 · Data presentation and Excel3 classes
A

Class A · Organising and summarising data

Frequency and percentage tables, bar and pie charts, class intervals and midpoints, estimated grouped means, and stem-and-leaf plots.

90 min
B

Class B · Distributions and relationships

Histograms, frequency polygons, cumulative tables and ogives; estimate medians, plot relationships, use a line of best fit and compare boxplots.

90 min
C

Class C · Campus café Excel practical

Use café data to build frequency tables, a bar chart, histogram and scatterplot in Excel; interpret the evidence and recommend how to reduce food waste.

90 min
Week 05 · Basic probability4 classes
A

Class A · Sets, events and Venn diagrams

Sample spaces, set notation, complements, intersections and unions; probability from diagrams.

90 min
B

Class B · Probability rules

Addition rules, mutually exclusive events and independence through worked and guided examples.

90 min
C

Class C · Applied probability practice

Use Venn diagrams and probability trees to solve multi-step problems and explain event relationships.

90 min
D

Class D · Tutorial: review, repair and prepare

Review descriptive statistics, charts and basic probability. Correct common errors through targeted questions and prepare for further probability work.

90 min
Week 06 · Probability and discrete distributions3 classes
A

Class A · Conditional probability and trees

Conditional probability, multiplication rules, independence and sampling with or without replacement.

90 min
B

Class B · Discrete random variables

Construct a probability distribution and calculate expected value and variance; introduce binomial conditions.

90 min
C

Class C · Probability workshop

Use dice and practical examples, calculate binomial probabilities and interpret mean and spread.

90 min
Week 07 · Continuous probability distributions3 classes
A

Class A · Continuous variables and probability area

Measurement scales, continuous random variables, rectangular density models and cumulative probability F(x).

90 min
B

Class B · Normal distribution and z-scores

Normal curve properties, standardisation and probabilities using the standard normal distribution.

90 min
C

Class C · Applying the normal model

Solve probability and percentile problems using guided examples and independent practice.

90 min
Week 08 · Statistical inference and estimation4 classes
A

Class A · Sampling distributions

Sampling variability, standard error and the Central Limit Theorem.

90 min
B

Class B · Confidence intervals

Point estimation, confidence levels, margin of error and intervals using z and t.

90 min
C

Class C · Estimation workshop

Calculate and interpret confidence intervals, compare precision and explain conclusions in context.

90 min
D

Class D · Tutorial: review, repair and prepare

Review probability distributions, normal calculations and estimation. Revisit difficult methods and practise interpreting results in context.

90 min
Week 09 · Hypothesis testing3 classes
A

Class A · Testing a claim

Null and alternative hypotheses, one- and two-tailed tests, significance levels and errors.

90 min
B

Class B · One-sample tests

Apply z-tests and t-tests, calculate test statistics and interpret p-values.

90 min
C

Class C · Hypothesis testing workshop

Select a method, work through a complete test and communicate an evidence-based conclusion.

90 min
Week 10 · Advanced hypothesis testing3 classes
A

Class A · Comparing two groups

Independent and paired samples; frame hypotheses and choose an appropriate test.

90 min
B

Class B · Two-sample and variance tests

Tests for population means with known or unknown variances; chi-square tests for population variance.

90 min
C

Class C · Comparison workshop

Practise paired and independent comparisons, interpret results and check assumptions.

90 min
Week 11 · Correlation and regression4 classes
A

Class A · Measuring relationships

Scatter plots, Pearson correlation and the distinction between association and causation.

90 min
B

Class B · Simple linear regression

Least-squares line, slope and intercept, predictions, model assumptions and R².

90 min
C

Class C · Regression workshop

Analyse data in Excel, interpret regression output and evaluate the limits of a prediction.

90 min
D

Class D · Tutorial: review, repair and prepare

Review hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Repair gaps in understanding and prepare for the mock assessment with targeted exam-style questions.

90 min
Week 12 · Revision and exam preparation3 classes
A

Class A · Descriptive statistics revision

Review sampling, summary measures, tables and graphs through mixed questions.

90 min
B

Class B · Probability and inference revision

Practise distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and regression; identify and correct common errors.

90 min
C

Class C · Mock assessment and feedback

Work through exam-style questions, explain methods and review solutions.

90 min

Course overview

Practice for Exam

Classes A, B and C every week; Class D tutorials in Weeks 2, 5, 8 and 11.

Level

Teaching weeks

Classes

corporate-finance.title: Corporate Finance · Jacob Mlynarski
corporate-finance.description: Explore Corporate Finance in 16 weekly classes: financial analysis, investment decisions, financing, working capital and integrated business cases.
corporate-finance.content:
Home / Courses / Corporate Finance

Corporate Finance

Business · Human Resource Management · Semester 1

Course InfoWhat You Will LearnCourse Content

About Course

Corporate Finance introduces the financial logic behind business decisions. In this 16-week course, you will explore how companies obtain funds, invest resources, manage daily operations and distribute profits, and how these choices affect company value.

We begin with financial statements and analysis, then develop the tools for valuing cash flows, understanding risk and evaluating investments. Later modules connect financing and capital structure with working capital and profit distribution. An integrated case and group presentation bring these decisions together before the final review.

Designed for Human Resource Management students, the course connects financial evidence with budgets, staffing investments, training proposals and operational trade-offs. Worked examples, guided calculations and group cases help you explain what the numbers mean and justify a recommendation.

What Will You Learn?

  • Explain the four financial decisions and interpret financial statements and ratios.
  • Apply time value of money and risk–return tools, including beta and CAPM.
  • Estimate project cash flows and evaluate investments using NPV, IRR and payback.
  • Compare financing sources, cost of capital and capital structure choices.
  • Analyse working capital, dividends, retained earnings and share repurchases.
  • Use financial evidence to defend a responsible business recommendation.

Course Content

5 modules · 16 classes

One 90-minute class each week, equivalent to two academic hours. The course comprises 32 academic hours across five modules and a final review.

Module 1 · Financial Foundations and Understanding Company Value3 classes
01

Class 01 · Introduction to Corporate Finance and Financial Decision Framework

Explore the purpose of corporate finance, distinguish the four financial decisions and explain how cash flow, time and risk affect company value.

90 min
02

Class 02 · Financial Statements: Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Cash Flow Statement

Read the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement, explain how they connect and distinguish accounting profit from cash flow.

90 min
03

Class 03 · Financial Analysis: Profitability, Liquidity, Efficiency, and Solvency

Calculate and interpret profitability, liquidity, efficiency and solvency ratios to assess financial performance and identify management priorities.

90 min
Module 2 · Value Creation and Investment Decisions4 classes
04

Class 04 · Time Value of Money: Compounding, Present Value, Future Value, and Annuities

Use cash-flow timelines, compounding and discounting to calculate present value, future value and annuities.

90 min
05

Class 05 · Risk and Return: Standard Deviation, Beta, CAPM, and Alpha Concept

Calculate expected return and standard deviation, explain diversification and interpret beta, CAPM required returns and alpha.

90 min
06

Class 06 · Investment Decisions: Capital Budgeting and Relevant Cash Flows

Identify incremental project cash flows, exclude sunk costs and account for opportunity costs, working capital and terminal cash flows.

90 min
07

Class 07 · Investment Evaluation: NPV, IRR, Payback, Sensitivity, and Scenario Analysis

Evaluate investments using payback, NPV and IRR, then test the recommendation through sensitivity and scenario analysis.

90 min
Module 3 · Financing Decisions and Capital Structure3 classes
08

Class 08 · Sources of Financing: Internal Funds, Debt, Equity, Bonds, Shares, and IPOs

Compare internal funds, debt and equity, including bonds, shares and IPOs, and weigh their effects on control, flexibility and risk.

90 min
09

Class 09 · Cost of Capital: Cost of Debt, Cost of Equity, CAPM, and WACC

Estimate the cost of debt and equity, calculate WACC and explain when it is suitable as a discount rate.

90 min
10

Class 10 · Capital Structure: Debt, Equity, Leverage, Financial Risk, and Optimal Mix

Assess debt–equity choices, leverage and financial distress to recommend a capital structure that balances risk and flexibility.

90 min
Module 4 · Operational Financial Management3 classes
11

Class 11 · Working Capital Management and the Cash Conversion Cycle

Analyse current assets and liabilities, calculate the cash conversion cycle and evaluate ways to improve liquidity.

90 min
12

Class 12 · Daily Financial Management: Cash, Inventory, Receivables, and EOQ Concept

project-management.title: Project Management · Jacob Mlynarski
project-management.description: Connect a project schedule with the decisions needed to deliver it and keep it on track.
project-management.content:
Home / Courses / Project Management

Project Management

Business · Business Administration · Semester 1

Course InfoWhat You Will LearnCourse Content

About Course

Project Management develops the methods needed to turn an idea into a planned, coordinated and controlled project. Across 16 classes, you will connect project objectives and customer requirements with scope, schedules, resources, costs and risk.

The course begins with identifying projects and developing proposals. You will then define work and responsibilities, build network diagrams and schedules, and analyse resource use and project performance. Later classes address risk, closure, leadership, teamwork and communication before the final review.

Worked examples, case analysis and collaborative tasks connect the tools to practical decisions. You will practise explaining trade-offs, documenting a plan and evaluating how a project is progressing.

What Will You Learn?

  • Define project objectives, deliverables, constraints and stakeholder needs.
  • Select projects and develop a proposal and project plan.
  • Create a work breakdown structure and assign responsibilities.
  • Build schedules, calculate slack and identify the critical path.
  • Plan resources and budgets, and analyse earned value and project performance.
  • Manage risks, communicate with stakeholders and evaluate project closure.

Course Content

5 modules · 16 classes

One class per teaching week, with two academic hours per class. The course comprises 32 academic hours, grouped into five modules and a final review.

Module 1 · Initiation and Project Proposals3 classes
01

Class 01 · Project Management Concepts

Define projects, objectives and deliverables; explore constraints, the project life cycle and stakeholder engagement.

2 acad. hrs
02

Class 02 · Identifying and Selecting Projects

Identify project opportunities, compare selection criteria and explain project charters and requests for proposals.

2 acad. hrs
03

Class 03 · Developing Project Proposals

Develop a proposal that connects the proposed solution, customer requirements, schedule and costs.

2 acad. hrs
Module 2 · Scope, Responsibilities and Scheduling5 classes
04

Class 04 · Defining Scope, Quality, Responsibility, and Activity Sequence · Part 1

Define scope and quality requirements, then break deliverables into work packages using a work breakdown structure.

2 acad. hrs
05

Class 05 · Defining Scope, Quality, Responsibility, and Activity Sequence · Part 2

Assign responsibility, define activities and arrange dependencies in a project network diagram.

2 acad. hrs
06

Class 06 · Developing the Schedule · Part 1

Estimate activity resources and durations, and calculate earliest start and finish times using a forward pass.

2 acad. hrs
07

Class 07 · Developing the Schedule · Part 2

Calculate latest start and finish times, determine slack and identify the critical path.

2 acad. hrs
08

Class 08 · Developing the Schedule · Part 3

Update schedules using actual progress and changes, and evaluate approaches to controlling project duration.

2 acad. hrs
Module 3 · Resources, Costs and Performance4 classes
09

Class 09 · Resource Utilization · Part 1

Identify resource constraints and prepare a resource requirements plan that supports the project schedule.

2 acad. hrs
10

Class 10 · Resource Utilization · Part 2

Apply resource leveling and compare schedules when available resources limit the work that can be completed.

2 acad. hrs
11

Class 11 · Determining Costs, Budget, and Earned Value · Part 1

Estimate activity costs, develop a time-phased baseline budget and determine the earned value of completed work.

2 acad. hrs
12

Class 12 · Determining Costs, Budget, and Earned Value · Part 2

Compare planned value, earned value and actual cost; interpret performance measures and forecast project costs.

2 acad. hrs
Module 4 · Risk Management and Project Closure1 class
13

Class 13 · Managing Risk and Closing the Project

Identify and prioritise risks, plan responses and monitoring, then review closure, customer feedback and lessons learned.

2 acad. hrs
Module 5 · Project Leadership and Communication2 classes
14

Class 14 · The Project Manager and the Project Team

Explore project-manager responsibilities, delegation, team development, conflict resolution and ethical teamwork.

2 acad. hrs
15

Class 15 · Project Communication and Documentation

Prepare a communication plan, facilitate meetings and present clear reports while controlling document changes.

2 acad. hrs
Course Review1 class
16

Class 16 · Summary

Connect the course concepts, review project-management methods and present an integrated account of project planning and control.

2 acad. hrs

Course overview

From project selection and planning to performance control, teamwork and closure.
